text.tspan: However, we've learned something more interesting: the best promoters don't necessarily
saturate the limits of their performance allowable by general principles. They are always
constrained by physical laws, but those might come up as system-dependent chemical rates.
To me, this says something about using arguments of optimization in biology. Their greatest
value is not to make quantitative predictions from optimality principles, but to force us to
confront the rich behavior arising from the real physical constraints biological systems
are subject to. This diversity may be biologically informative and interesting in its own right.
